en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the course is to theoretically and practically clarify the principles and technological procedures of forest establishment in different ecotopes.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Legislative regulations on forest regeneration (allowance 0/2) a.Sources of forest reproductive materialb.Legislative limits in forest regeneration2.General principles of forest regeneration (allowance 6/12) a.Natural and artificial forest regenerationb.Forest establishment by sowingc.Forest establishment by plantingd.Spacing and density of plantatione.Establishment of mixed forest stands3.Site preparation for forest regeneration (allowance 2/0) a.Mechanical site preparationb.Chemical site preparationc.Biological site preparation4.Forest seed management (allowance 2/0) a.Collection of forest seed materialb.Handling and processing seed materialc.Seed storaged.Pre-sowing treatment5.Forest nurseries (allowance 2/0) a.Types of forest planting stockb.Types of forest nurseriesc.Establishment of nurseries on forest land and on other than forest land6.Forest regeneration on main types of sites (allowance 4/0) a.Forest regeneration on sandy and dry hanitatsb.Reforestation of heavily weeded localitiesc.Reforestation in habitats exposed to frostd.Reforestation of high mountain localitiese.Reforestation of wet habitatsf.Reforestation after disasters7.Care of plantings (allowance 6/10) a.Minimization of game damageb.Minimization the negative impact of weedsc.Minimization of damage by biotic agentsd.Minimization of damage by abiotic agents
